newsitem.title: USA: Health Risk, Health Plan end merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Health Risk, Health Plan end merger plan.

text.p: Health Risk Management Inc and HealthPlan Services Corp said Thurday they mutually decided to end their previously announced merger agreement.
The companies also said that Health Plan had agreed to acquire 200,000 unregistered shares of Health Risk, or about 4.5 percent of its shares outstanding, at a price of $12.50 a share.
William Bennett, chairman of HealthPlan, said the stock was purchased for investment purposes.
The companies also said they committed to continue to market jointly their respective products and services, under the terms of a marketing agreement set in September 1996.

"While we are naturally disappointed that we were unable to pursue a merger at this time, we look forward to the business opportunity to offer our customers access to (Health Risk's) innovative and cost effective products, including its demand management services and practice guidelines software," William Bennett, chairman of HealthPlan, said in a statement.
Gary McIlroy, chairman of Health Risk Management, said he welcomed HealthPlan as a shareholder.
"We have already added three new contractual relationships through our relationship with (HealthPlan), and we anticipate similar success in the future," McIlroy added.

The companies said they agreed to terminate the merger agreement because of the delay caused by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission review process. They added they were unwilling to consummate a transaction that might be of less value and dilutive to their respective shareholders in the near term.

Health Risk provides total health benefit management, health care claim management and health care information technologies to self-insured employers, health maintenance organizations, insurance companies, hospitals, governmental entities, and others.
HealthPlan Services provides managed care services to over 125,000 small businesses and large, self-insured organizations.
